blocks.text: R&D

Scientific research is one of the most critical fields of activity for the faculty, postgraduate students, and undergraduate students of the University. Conducting research ensures the continuous improvement of the educational and training process through fundamental and applied research in existing fields of study, as well as the implementation of modern methodologies and pedagogical technologies into educational practice.
Objectives of Research and Development Work
• Conducting relevant and timely scientific research;
• Enriching the educational process with the results of the latest scientific research;
• Providing students and faculty members with practical exposure to the setup of scientific studies and engaging them in the execution of research projects;
• Upgrading the academic and scientific qualifications of the teaching staff;
• Training highly qualified academic and pedagogical staff;
writing and preparing for publication textbooks, teaching aids, monographs, scientific articles and reports;
editing textbooks, teaching aids, monographs, scientific articles and reports;
management of student and scientific circles.
• Providing information and resource support for the university library;
• Collaborating with national scientific publications and journals.
Main Fields of Research and Development Work
• Developing scientific and theoretical problems;
• Solving the most pressing issues in the fields of economics, social sciences, humanities, and information technologies, as well as in domestic and foreign science;
• Studying and synthesizing the R&D experiences of other higher education institutions, research institutes, and organizations;
• Publishing textbooks and study guides;
• Executing research projects of a scientific and methodological nature.
University Support for R&D Activities
• Provides all necessary informational support for R&D;
• Manages the preparation and publication of monographs, textbooks, study guides, collections of scientific papers, and other academic publications;
• Organizes international, regional, and interuniversity conferences and seminars hosted at the University;
• Ensures the effective functioning of Student Research & Development Activities (SRDA).
Internet resources and other multimedia sources are actively integrated into these processes.

The student community of the University serves as the primary base for research and development activities. Scientific research and methodological work are carried out in alignment with comprehensive and individual research topics developed by university departments and individual instructors, as well as part of the continuous improvement of the institution's educational activities.

Annual planning, execution, and evaluation of R&D results are reflected in the individual plans of each instructor. These are then aggregated into the annual plans and reports of departments and faculties for this specific type of activity.
Organization of Research and Development Work at BSU

BSU participates in implementing its research results into practice and actively promotes the achievements of domestic science, technology, and culture. It conducts scientific research by coordinating R&D plans, organizing collaborative scientific studies, and co-hosting scientific conferences.
• Research and development works at BSU are carried out in accordance with a plan reviewed by the University Academic Council and approved by the Rector.

• The university's research plans are developed with the active participation of faculties and departments. Research work at the University is conducted by professors, associate professors, instructors, etc.
• The Heads of Departments and Deans of Faculties bear direct responsibility for the execution of the research work plan within their respective departments and faculties.
• Heads of Departments submit progress and final R&D reports to the Vice-Rector for Research.
• The university regularly publishes scientific papers and collections of proceedings from scientific conferences.
